title: In 2 Kings 6 How Can We Apply The Lesson Of Spiritual Sight From Elishas Prayer To Our Own Lives
paragraphs: The Lesson of Spiritual Sight in 2 Kings 6: Elisha’s Prayer and Its Application Today

The story in 2 Kings 6 is a remarkable account of God’s power and the importance of spiritual vision. Here, the prophet Elisha prays for his servant’s eyes to be opened so he can see the spiritual reality that surrounds them. This episode challenges us to consider what it means to truly “see” by faith and how we can develop spiritual sight in our daily walk with God.
The Biblical Account: Elisha and the Army of Angels
When the king of Syria sends an army to capture Elisha, his servant is fearful upon seeing the city surrounded by horses and chariots. Elisha reassures him:
And he answered, Fear not; for they that are with us are more than they that are with them. - 2 Kings 6:16 ASV
Then Elisha prays:

And Elisha prayed, and said, Jehovah, I pray thee, open his eyes, that he may see. And Jehovah opened the eyes of the young man; and he saw: and, behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha. - 2 Kings 6:17 ASV
God reveals to the servant an unseen spiritual reality: a heavenly army protecting them.
Key Insights and Applications
Spiritual Sight vs. Physical Sight
The servant saw only danger with his natural eyes, but Elisha saw God's protection. The New Testament echoes this principle:
for we walk by faith, not by sight - 2 Corinthians 5:7 ASV
As believers, we are called to trust in the unseen promises and presence of God, not merely in what we perceive physically.
Prayer for Spiritual Vision
Elisha did not try to convince his servant with arguments; he prayed for God to open his eyes. Likewise, we need to seek God’s help to perceive spiritual truths. Paul prays similarly for believers:
having the eyes of your heart enlightened, that ye may know what is the hope of his calling... - Ephesians 1:18 ASV
We should regularly ask God to open our spiritual eyes to His reality and purposes.
Confidence in God's Sovereignty
Elisha’s calmness came from knowing God’s power and presence. In the face of trials, we can find peace by remembering:
And we know that to them that love God all things work together for good, even to them that are called according to his purpose. - Romans 8:28 ASV
Spiritual sight gives us confidence to face adversity, recognizing that God is always at work, even when we cannot see it.
Seeing Others Through God's Eyes

Just as Elisha saw with spiritual insight, we should ask God to help us see people and circumstances not only as they appear, but as God sees them. Christ models this in his compassion and insight into people’s hearts (Matthew 9:36 ASV).
Practical Steps to Cultivate Spiritual Sight
Abide in God’s Word: Regular study of Scripture sharpens our spiritual discernment (Psalm 119:18 ASV).
Commit to Prayer: Ask God daily to open your eyes to His work and to give you wisdom in every situation (James 1:5 ASV).
Walk by Faith: Choose to trust God’s promises, even when circumstances seem daunting (Hebrews 11:1 ASV).
Fellowship with Believers: Surround yourself with others who will encourage you and help you see God’s perspective.
Conclusion

The lesson of 2 Kings 6 challenges us to look beyond our circumstances and to seek God’s perspective. As we pray for spiritual sight, trust in God’s Word, and rely on the Holy Spirit, we can face life’s challenges with confidence, assured that “those who are with us are more than those who are with them.” Let us, like Elisha, pray that God would open our eyes to see His presence and power at work in every situation.
